title: Marcos concludes 3-day China trip for APEC 2026 summit
summary: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Friday afternoon flew back to Manila after wrapping up his three-day visit in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Conference (APEC) Economic Leaders'…

blocks.text: SHENZHEN, China — President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Friday afternoon flew back to Manila after wrapping up his three-day visit in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Conference (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting.
The PR001 carrying the President and his delegation left Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport at 4:13 p.m.
They are expected to land in Villamor Air Base in Pasay City at about 6 p.m.

Before departing Shenzhen, Marcos held a Kapihan forum with the Philippine media where he said he used his presence in the APEC summit "to the maximum" by meeting with world leaders as well as business executives.

"So that the opportunities that a conference like APEC provides are fully utilized and we can find ways to engage new partners around the world in the hope that those engagements will bring new business, bring new trade to the betterment of our economy," the President said.

On the sidelines of the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, Marcos had pull-aside meetings with New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, Vietnamese President To Lam, and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum.
He also had bilateral meetings with Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast, Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori, and Papua New Guinea Prime Minister James Marape.

On Friday, Marcos also led business meetings with Chinese manufacturing company C&U Group, electric vehicle manufacturer BYD Company Limited, and clean-energy technology company Ming Yang Smart Energy Group Limited. — VDV, GMA News
